extracted.intended_audience: parties, counsel, applicants, licensees, NRC staff, and presiding officers involved in NRC adjudicatory proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements governing settlements, initial decisions, review, stays, petitions, ex parte communications, and separation of functions in NRC adjudicatory proceedings under 10 CFR part 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of ongoing settlement negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: The conduct of settlement negotiations does not divest the presiding officer of jurisdiction and does not automatically stay the proceeding. A hearing must not be unduly delayed because of the conduct of settlement negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: A settlement must be in the form of a proposed settlement agreement, a consent order, and a motion for its entry that includes the reasons why it should be accepted. It must be signed by the consenting parties or their authorized representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of settlement agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed settlement agreement must contain: (1) an admission of all jurisdictional facts; (2) an express waiver of further procedural steps before the presiding officer, of any right to challenge or contest the validity of the order entered in accordance with the agreement, and of all rights to seek judicial review or otherwise to contest the validity of the consent order; (3) a statement that the order has the same force and effect as an order made after full hearing; and (4) a statement that matters identified in the agreement, required to be adjudicated have been resolved by the proposed settlement agreement and consent order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All four elements are required in the proposed settlement agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of settlement agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Following issuance of a notice of hearing, a settlement must be approved by the presiding officer or the Commission as appropriate to be binding. The presiding officer or Commission may order adjudication of issues if required in the public interest. In enforcement proceedings under subpart B, the presiding officer shall accord due weight to the position of the NRC staff when reviewing the settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved, terms must be embodied in a decision or order; settlements approved by a presiding officer are subject to Commission review under § 2.341.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited decisionmaking — omission or immediate effectiveness of initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may determine a proceeding by order after the conclusion of a hearing without issuing an initial decision, or may make an initial decision effective immediately, only when: (1) all parties stipulate and waive rights to petition for review, oral argument, and judicial review; (2) no unresolved substantial issue of fact, law, or discretion remains and the record clearly warrants relief; and (3) the presiding officer finds dispensing with or making immediate the initial decision is in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An order entered under the omission provision is subject to Commission review on its own motion within 40 days; an immediately effective initial decision is subject to Commission review on its own motion within 30 days. Certain authorizations (listed in § 2.339(d)) are excluded from these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer initial decision — findings on matters put into controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: In contested proceedings (operating licenses, combined licenses, manufacturing licenses, and other proceedings), the presiding officer shall make findings of fact and conclusions of law on the matters put into controversy by the parties and on any matter designated by the Commission to be decided by the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer may also make findings on matters not put in controversy only to the extent the presiding officer determines a serious safety, environmental, or common defense and security matter exists and the Commission approves examination and decision on the matter (referral under §§ 2.323 and 2.341).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer decision — consideration of matters not put in controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall make findings on matters not put in controversy only to the extent the presiding officer determines a serious safety, environmental, or common defense and security matter exists and the Commission approves of examination and decision on the matter upon referral by the presiding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such referred matters may be treated by the Commission as a request for action under § 2.206 and processed under § 52.103(f) or § 53.1452(f) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of permits, licenses, and amendments following initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After an initial decision becomes effective, the Commission or the appropriate Director shall issue, deny, or appropriately condition the permit, license, or amendment in accordance with the presiding officer's initial decision, subject to the timing and exceptions set forth for different license types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some cases (e.g., where the NRC has made a determination of no significant hazards consideration or under specific provisions § 2.1202(a) or § 2.1403(a)), the appropriate official may issue an amendment before the initial decision becomes effective; if the initial decision becomes effective first, action must be taken in accordance with that decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effectiveness of certain presiding officer decisions (types listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer's initial decision directing issuance or amendment of specified authorizations (limited work authorizations, early site permits, construction permits/authorizations, operating licenses, combined licenses, manufacturing licenses, renewed licenses, licenses under part 72 to store spent fuel, licenses under part 61, or initial decisions under § 52.103(g) or § 53.1452(g)) is immediately effective upon issuance unless the presiding officer finds good cause shown by a party why it should not be immediately effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of affected authorizations is extensive and must be checked in the regulation text when relying on immediate effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance timeline for authorizations, permits, and licenses (10-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or appropriate Director shall issue specified authorizations, permits, or licenses within 10 days from the date of issuance of the initial decision if: (1) the Commission/Director has made all findings necessary for issuance not within the scope of the presiding officer's initial decision; and (2) issuance proceeds notwithstanding the pendency of petitions for reconsideration, review, motions for stay, or § 2.206 filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 10-day issuance requirement is applied to production/utilization facilities, combined licenses, manufacturing licenses, and other licenses as specified in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of finding on acceptance criteria (10-day rule for § 52.103 / § 53.1452)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or appropriate Director shall make the finding under § 52.103(g) or § 53.1452(g) that acceptance criteria in a combined license are met within 10 days from the presiding officer's initial decision date, subject to specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include ability to make the finding for criteria not within presiding officer's initial decision and presiding officer findings that criteria have been or will be met; applies notwithstanding pending petitions or motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of presiding officer decisions — Commission own-motion review timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may review decisions or actions of a presiding officer on its own motion within 120 days after the date of the decision or action, or within 120 days after a petition for review has been served, unless the Commission extends the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section does not apply to certain appeals (e.g., § 2.311 appeals) or high-level waste proceedings governed by § 2.1015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for review — filing time, page limits, and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file a petition for review with the Commission within 25 days after service of a full or partial initial decision (or other decisions/actions for which review is authorized). A petition for review may not be longer than thirty (30) pages and must contain: (i) a concise summary of the decision or action; (ii) a statement (with record citation) where the matters were previously raised before the presiding officer or why they could not have been raised; (iii) a concise statement why the decision/action is erroneous; and (iv) a concise statement why Commission review should be exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise authorized by law, a party must file a petition for Commission review before seeking judicial review of an agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answers and reply briefs on petitions for review — length and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other party may, within 25 days after service of a petition for review, file an answer supporting or opposing review (not longer than 25 pages). The petitioning party may file a reply brief within 10 days of service of any answer (reply may not be longer than 5 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers should concisely address the petition contents to the extent appropriate; page limits exclude tables of contents/citations when specified elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for granting a petition for review
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition for review may be granted in the Commission's discretion, giving due weight to the existence of a substantial question with respect to: (i) a finding of material fact that is clearly erroneous or in conflict with a finding in another proceeding; (ii) a necessary legal conclusion that lacks governing precedent or departs from established law; (iii) a substantial and important question of law, policy, or discretion; (iv) prejudicial procedural error in the proceeding; or (v) any other consideration the Commission deems in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition will not be granted to the extent it relies on matters that could have been but were not raised before the presiding officer; matters raised sua sponte by the presiding officer count as raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A ruling referred or question certified to the Commission may be reviewed if it raises significant and novel legal or policy issues or resolution would materially advance orderly disposition. The Commission may also grant interlocutory review at a party's request absent referral/certification if the party demonstrates the issue: (i) threatens immediate and serious irreparable impact not alleviable through later review; or (ii) affects the basic structure of the proceeding in a pervasive or unusual manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition and answer for interlocutory review must be filed within the times and in the form prescribed for petitions for review and treated under the general provisions of § 2.341.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief length limits on Commission review
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the Commission orders otherwise, any briefs on review may not exceed 30 pages in length, exclusive of pages containing the table of contents, table of citations, and any addendum with exhibits, statutes, or regulations. A brief in excess of 10 pages must contain a table of contents with page references and a tables of cases/statutes/authorities with references to where they are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stays of decisions — filing time and exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Within ten (10) days after service of a decision or action of a presiding officer, any party may file an application for a stay of effectiveness pending filing of and decision on a petition for review. This application may be filed with the Commission or the presiding officer, but not both at the same time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay application content and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a stay may be no longer than ten (10) pages, exclusive of affidavits, and must contain: (1) a concise summary of the decision/action requested to be stayed; (2) a concise statement of the grounds for stay with reference to factors specified in paragraph (e); and (3) where reliance is on disputed facts, appropriate references to the record or affidavits by knowledgeable persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and answers for stay applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of a stay application on other parties must be by the same method as filing. Within ten (10) days after service, any party may file an answer supporting or opposing the stay; the answer may not be longer than ten (10) pages exclusive of affidavits. Further replies will not be entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing/service methods (electronic, facsimile, mail) must match filing with Commission or presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in deciding stay applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether to grant or deny a stay, the Commission or presiding officer will consider: (1) whether the moving party has made a strong showing it is likely to prevail on the merits; (2) whether the party will be irreparably injured unless a stay is granted; (3) whether granting a stay would harm other parties; and (4) where the public interest lies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In extraordinary cases, a temporary stay may be granted promptly (even orally) to preserve status quo, subject to prompt written confirmation and reasonable effort to inform other parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument before the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may allow oral argument in its discretion upon request in a petition for review, brief on review, or upon its own initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the Commission final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The final decision will be in writing and will include: (1) a statement of findings and conclusions with the basis for them on all material issues of fact, law, or discretion presented; (2) all facts officially noticed; (3) the ruling on each material issue; and (4) the appropriate ruling, order, or denial of relief, with the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will ordinarily consider the whole record on review but may limit issues to those identified in an order taking review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reconsideration of final decision — timing and standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition for reconsideration of a final decision must be filed by a party within ten (10) days after the date of the decision. The petition must demonstrate a compelling circumstance, such as the existence of a clear and material error in a decision, which could not have been reasonably anticipated, which renders the decision invalid, and must state the relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other party may file an answer in opposition or support within ten (10) days; filing or granting of such a petition does not stay the decision unless the Commission orders otherwise. Petitions for reconsideration of Commission decisions granting or denying review in whole or in part will not be entertained (see § 2.341(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of the Secretary for procedural matters
rubrics_metrics.description: When briefs, motions, or other documents are submitted to the Commission itself, the Secretary or Assistant Secretary is authorized to: prescribe procedures for filing when schedules differ from rules; rule on motions for extensions of time; reject late filings unless good cause is shown; prescribe procedural arrangements for oral argument; extend times for Commission action on petitions for review or own-motion review; direct improperly filed pleadings to the appropriate presiding officer; deny requests for hearings that fail to comply with pleading requirements and fail to set forth an arguable basis; refer requests for hearings to the ASLBP or Administrative Judge where appropriate; and take action on other minor matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary's authority governs procedural scheduling, acceptance/rejection of filings, and other ministerial tasks related to filings before the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications — prohibition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons outside the agency may not make or knowingly cause to be made to any Commission adjudicatory employee any ex parte communication relevant to the merits of the proceeding. Commission adjudicatory employees may not request or entertain from any interested person outside the agency, or make to any interested person outside the agency, any ex parte communication relevant to the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this section, 'merits of the proceeding' includes: (i) a disputed issue; (ii) a matter which a presiding officer seeks to be referred to the Commission under § 2.340(a); and (iii) a matter for which the Commission has approved examination by the presiding officer under § 2.340(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications — recordation and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Commission adjudicatory employee who receives, makes, or knowingly causes to be made a communication prohibited by this section shall ensure that it, and any responses, are promptly served on the parties and placed in the public record. For oral communications, a written summary must be served and placed in the public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt of a communication knowingly made or caused by a party in violation, the Commission or other adjudicatory employee may require the party to show cause why its claim or interest should not be dismissed, denied, disregarded, or otherwise adversely affected on account of the violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications — applicability and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibitions apply when a notice of hearing or comparable order is issued or when the interested person or adjudicatory employee knows such an order will be issued. The prohibitions cease to apply to ex parte communications relevant to the merits of a full or partial initial decision when the time has expired for Commission review of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: (1) requests for and provision of status reports; (2) communications specifically permitted by statute or regulation; (3) communications to or by Commission adjudicatory employees in the Office of the General Counsel regarding matters pending before a court or another agency; (4) communications regarding generic issues involving public health and safety or other statutory responsibilities of the agency not associated with resolution of any proceeding under this subpart; and (5) communications in contested and uncontested mandatory proceedings regarding an undisputed issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions — prohibition on investigative/litigating staff participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any NRC officer or employee engaged in investigative or litigating functions in a proceeding or a factually related proceeding with respect to a disputed issue may not participate in or advise a Commission adjudicatory employee about the initial or final decision with respect to that disputed issue, except as (1) witness or counsel in the proceeding; (2) through a written communication served on all parties and made on-the-record; or (3) through an oral communication made with reasonable prior notice to all parties and reasonable opportunity for response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions — exceptions and permitted communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition does not apply to communications to or from Commission adjudicatory employees regarding the status of a proceeding; matters specifically permitted by statute or regulation; NRC participation in matters pending before a court or another agency; or generic issues involving public health and safety not associated with resolution of a proceeding. It also does not apply to communications to or from Commissioners, certain staff, and specified offices regarding initiation/direction of investigations, supervision of NRC staff, staff priorities/schedules, allocation of resources, or general regulatory/scientific/engineering principles not contested in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of the communications permitted by these subparagraphs is to be associated by the Commission adjudicatory employee or the NRC officer or employee performing investigative or litigating functions with the resolution of any proceeding under this subpart pending before the NRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions — public record requirement for prohibited communications received
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Commission adjudicatory employee who receives a communication prohibited under the separation-of-functions prohibition shall ensure that it, and any responses to it, are placed in the public record of the proceeding and served on the parties.
